Frugal and budget experts please recommend some books for a family that needs to get out of debt.

I really don't think there's a book out there that will tell you anything other than "learn the legal side of things, understand your obligations, and save money where you can." Most of us cann't help you with the first two, but we can help you with the saving money bit. It would help if we knew you, because then we could tell you where you could save money specifically, but we can still give you some good tips. My advice to you is to just start perusing posts, and you'll probably come back with a few different things that can help you divert more of your money to paying off debt.

There's no secret. I always tell my children that their money gets away from them in small ways...pennies at a time. Being responsible with $ is a way of life. Always live Below your means, never buy ridiculous wasteful items like bottled water. Drink water when you eat out. Never buy lunch out when you work away from home, not as a regular thing, take leftovers, an apple from home anything to keep from buying lunch. Never, ever as Long as you Live should you buy a drink from a vending machine, bring a can from home. Turn down the thermostat in the winter, and always when you leave home for the day. I wouldn't be caught dead buying a Starbucks coffee...and I can well afford it! It's just little pennies that add up to dollars.

If you haven't read it, pick up a copy of "The Richest Man in Babylon."

I have spent years working on my own debt issues, participated in many an Internet forum, and this book is one I kept on the shelf and revisited many times if for no other reason than moral support in hard times.

The book is NOT religious in nature, but the author uses parables as a storytelling style. Some "get out of debt" books are full of charts and interest calculations, and practical advice. However TRMIB addresses a much more thorough set of inter-related topics, such as how debt is like slavery, the freedom that comes from saving (even a little) money of your own, to attitudes about work, pride, employer/employee relationships, and even how to compartmentalize your debts so that you can still live your life. I have gifted this book to family members and never hesitate to mention it when asked.

Best of luck to you.
